summary: Short year-end procurement sync focused on outstanding DPA redlines, KMS keying approach, VPC/connectivity preflight and a quick cost/latency tradeoff discussion for a pilot. AE + SE present; legal + procurement + infra from customer. Agreed to exchange redlines, run a connectivity smoke test, and reconvene in early Jan for procurement sign-off.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-24 09:30 PST, Duration 38m. Attendees: Evan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Liam Carter (AcmePay Legal), Sara Nguyen (AcmePay Procurement), Tom Reyes (AcmePay Infra), Juno Park (AcmePay Security).
00:00 Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining at short notice, appreciate it on a holiday week. Quick objective — close out the DPA questions and confirm keying and connectivity so procurement can route the MSA next week.
00:22 Liam: Thanks, Evan. I'll be short, had our counsel skim the DPA, there are three sticking points — data residency carveouts, subprocessors list, and indemnity caps tied to egress.
00:37 Evan: Got it, that's pretty standard. Priya, quick reminder on how Redwood handles subprocessors —
00:45 Priya: Yeah so we publish the subprocessors list, and for private deployments we can offer a limited subproc list. FYI our private offering is sometimes called Redwood Privatee in older docs, ignore that, that's a doc typo. Also, for hosted we have SOC2 plus contractual commitments.
01:05 Tom: One thing from infra — egress fees. If we keep everything in-region and do dedicated pooling are egresss costs reduced? We saw a line item with BigCloudAI that spiked.
01:20 Priya: Two parts — routing and placement. If you use Dedicated capacity or private VPC peering, egress to your VPC is generally minimal; cross-region traffic will incur cloud egress. For hosted endpoints there is more routing that could add cost. We can map your expected token volumes to a cost projection.
01:42 Sara: For procurement, timeline is tight. We need the annotated DPA and an idea of monthly burn for a 3-month pilot before routing to finance. Also any notes on SSO and SAML requirements.
01:55 Evan: We'll send annotated DPA redlines. On SAML/SSO we support SSO via SAML and OIDC, SSO integration is in the onboarding playbook.
02:10 Liam: KMS — primary question: who holds the keys? We prefer customer-managed keys, maybe HSM-backed. Does Redwood support a bring-your-own-key flow?
02:22 Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS through standard cloud KMS and also have an HSM integration for our Private packages. For hosted with customer-managed keys there's a path but with certain limitations on replay and cache; we need to align on key rotation windows because KV cache and session-state require ephemeral caching.
02:47 Juno: When you say cache, do you mean KV cache? We worry about plaintext tokens in cache if keys rotate mid-session.
02:56 Priya: Good callout. Our runtime encrypts KV cache at rest with the active key; when rotation happens we rewrap the data — small window but not left as plaintext. There are some legacy docs that say re-encrypt, sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in notes, so apologies for confusions.
03:20 Tom: Can we do a quick network diagram? We have VPC in us-west-2, want peering or private link? The diagram will affect firewall rules and procurement checklist.
03:32 Priya: We'll draw it up. For low-latency use we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud provider; peering tends to be simpler but PrivateLink gives more control and smaller attack surface. We'll include the connectivity checklist in the deck.
03:50 Sara: About SLAs — what does Redwood guarantee for hosted vs dedicated? Finance will want an SLA number for downtime and P95 latency.
04:02 Evan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort but we publish performance profiles. For pilot we can offer a service availability target and an escalation path; contractual SLAs get added at commit.
04:22 Liam: Indemnity and liability cap — our counsel is pushing for a reciprocal liability cap tied to fees. Any flexibility?
04:32 Evan: We can discuss tiered caps based on committed spend for Dedicated. For hosted pilots it's more standard but we can propose a limited carveout. We'll highlight options in the next DPA iteration.
04:47 Sara: Pricing — we need a 3-month estimate. Last time we saw a token-based pricing example but wanted committed monthly throughput pricing for the pilot.
05:00 Priya: We have two pilot models: usage-based with a discount band, or a small committed capacity pool (Dedicated burst) that sets a predictable monthly fee. For latency-sensitive routes we recommend dedicated for that route; cheaper background workloads can be hosted.
05:25 Tom: Any competitor comparatives on performance we should know about? BigCloudAI's pricing was lower but latency was worse.
05:33 Evan: Competitors mentioned — BigCloudAI tends to undercut but adds variability; ModelServeX claims on-premise-only but their orchestration is heavier; NimbusOps has a similar dedicated product. We can share a short benchmark table.
05:56 Liam: One legal nit — audit logs. We need immutable audit logs for key access and data exfil events. Is that available?
06:07 Priya: Yes, we provide audit logs at token route level and admin actions. For Private deployments audits are customer-controlled; for hosted we stream logs to your S3/secure bucket if you want. We also support SIEM integrations.
06:26 Juno: Are those logs encrypted at rest and do you support retention policies?
06:32 Priya: Encrypted at rest, retention configurable; we'll include retention defaults and how to change them.
06:40 Sara: Quick question on subprocessors — will Redwood accept a clause to notify for new subprocessors 30 days in advance?
06:51 Evan: We can commit to notice for major changes; full contractual terms we'll propose in DPA redlines.
07:05 Liam: Regarding data residency, we need a clause that PII for EU customers stays in eu-west-1. Does Redwood allow strict regional tenancy?
07:17 Priya: For Dedicated and Private yes you can pin model serving to regions; for hosted we can make best-effort routing but can't guarantee strict tenancy unless you sign up for a Private deployment or reserved Dedicated capacity in-region. We'll make that explicit.
07:38 Tom: On the technical side, Priya, can you run a two-hour connectivity smoke test to validate peering? We can open short windows over the holidays.
07:50 Priya: I can run a 30–60 minute quick test this week and then schedule a longer test Jan 5. We'll need access tokens and a temporary staging VPC endpoint.
08:05 Evan: Logistics — I'll drop the annotated DPA and a connectivity checklist into the shared folder by end of day Jan 3. Priya will run the first smoke test and share results. Juno will decide on KMS approach. Liam will summarize legal exceptions.
08:25 Sara: Procurement is OK to do a conditional purchase order for the pilot pending final DPA and connectivity success; helps speed finance routing.
08:36 Evan: Great. Any other blockers?
08:40 Liam: Nothing else from legal, we'll wait for redlines.
08:45 Tom: I'll work on firewall rules and share with Priya.
08:49 Juno: I'll confirm KMS options with our security vendor.
08:52 Evan: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene early Jan. Happy holidays.
08:58 All: Happy holidays, thanks.
